summary: Extends LDAP with absolute True and False filters, based on capabilities in X.500, and extends the string form of search filters to support them. It is a proposed standard.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 4526 adds two LDAP search filters that always return the same result: (&) is True and (|) is False. A client should use them only when it knows the server supports the feature.

subtitle: LDAP filters that always evaluate to True or False, written (&) and (|).

tldr.problem: LDAPv3's search-filter forms could not express empty AND and OR sets, which prevented direct use of absolute True and False filters.
tldr.mechanism: The extension allows an empty AND filter to evaluate as True and an empty OR filter to evaluate as False, with string forms (&) and (|).
tldr.outcome: The filters support a more direct mapping between DAP and LDAP, and clients should use them only when the server supports the feature.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 4526's status as Proposed Standard. It extends LDAP search filters with empty AND and OR forms.

sections.title: Why Empty Filters Are Useful
sections.content:
X.500 directory access supports absolute True and False assertions. An AND filter with no elements is always True, and an OR filter with no elements is always False.

LDAPv3 removed these cases because the LDAPv2 string representation could not express empty AND or OR sets. This extension restores them so a DAP-to-LDAP gateway can map filters more directly.
sections.plainLanguage: An empty AND or OR filter can represent a result that is always true or always false. This extension lets LDAP express those cases again.

sections.title: The Two Absolute Filters
sections.content:
Implementations of the extension must allow AND and OR choices with zero filter elements. An empty AND filter evaluates to True and is written (&); an empty OR filter evaluates to False and is written (|).

A server supporting the feature should publish its feature identifier in the root DSE. A client should not use the feature unless it knows that the server supports it.
sections.plainLanguage: The filter (&) always matches, while (|) never matches. Clients should check that the server supports these forms before sending them.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC does not believe that reintroducing absolute True and False filters raises new security considerations. It directs implementers to the general security considerations for LDAPv3.

This extension does not change the requirements for search operations that require particular filters, such as operations used to retrieve subschema information.
sections.plainLanguage: The new filter forms do not change the security rules for LDAP. Some searches still have to use the filters required by their own specifications.
